cards.statement: Self-supervised pre-training derives prediction targets directly from a language model's input text.
cards.explanation: A language model learns from patterns in its text corpus, such as predicting the next token from preceding text. The training text supplies the target as well as the context.

source.title: What are Foundation Models?

cards.statement: Continued pre-training adapts an FM using labeled examples of tasks paired with their desired answers.
cards.explanation: Continued pre-training uses additional unlabeled text to strengthen a model's domain knowledge. Task-specific labeled examples belong to supervised fine-tuning.
cards.misconception: Continued pre-training uses the task-answer supervision associated with fine-tuning.

source.title: Fine-tuning large language models in healthcare

cards.statement: Instruction tuning helps a model apply learned task patterns to instructions absent from its training examples.
cards.explanation: Training across varied instruction-based tasks improves general instruction following. A model uses related learned concepts when it encounters a new task prompt.

source.title: Zero-shot prompting for the Flan-T5 foundation model in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

cards.statement: Transfer learning starts a related task by replacing a model's learned weights with random values.
cards.explanation: Transfer learning starts from a pre-trained model and retains useful knowledge from earlier training. It adapts those learned representations to a related target task.
cards.misconception: Transfer learning resets the previously learned model rather than reusing it.

source.title: What is Transfer Learning?

cards.statement: Model distillation transfers a teacher model's learned weights directly to a smaller student model.
cards.explanation: A student learns from response examples produced by a teacher. Distillation passes behavioral knowledge through training data rather than copying the teacher's weights.
cards.misconception: Distillation copies a teacher's internal weights into the student instead of training the student from teacher responses.

source.title: Customize a model with distillation in Amazon Bedrock

cards.statement: RLHF trains its reward model to reproduce ideal answers written by human reviewers.
cards.explanation: An RLHF reward model learns to score responses according to human preferences. Its scores guide training toward behavior that people prefer.
cards.misconception: An RLHF reward model learns to generate human-written target answers instead of scoring response preferences.

source.title: Fine-tune large language models with reinforcement learning from human or AI feedback

cards.statement: Fine-tuning treats a training example's user request as the style target for the generated response.
cards.explanation: The desired assistant answers demonstrate the style and output format a fine-tuned model learns. User requests provide inputs; the corresponding responses show how the business wants the model to answer.
cards.misconception: The user request's writing style serves as the desired output-style target during fine-tuning.

source.title: Preparing data for supervised fine-tuning Part 1: Formatting and quality

cards.statement: AI teams include paraphrased requests in fine-tuning data to improve handling of varied user phrasing.
cards.explanation: A model trained on a narrow request wording may struggle with another phrasing of the same intent. Representative examples teach it how to respond across the application's actual request wording.

source.title: Preparing data for supervised fine-tuning Part 1: Formatting and quality

cards.statement: Multi-turn fine-tuning treats a follow-up answer as independent of earlier messages in the example.
cards.explanation: Multi-turn training examples preserve earlier user and assistant exchanges. Those exchanges supply the context needed to produce a coherent follow-up response.
cards.misconception: A multi-turn training example trains each follow-up in isolation from the preceding dialogue.

source.title: Prepare data for fine-tuning your models

cards.statement: Narrow domain fine-tuning exposes an FM to the risk of losing its earlier task capabilities.
cards.explanation: Catastrophic forgetting occurs when new training overwrites useful prior capabilities. Domain specialization can therefore reduce performance outside the new training focus.

source.title: Preparing data for supervised fine-tuning Part 2: Advanced data strategies

cards.statement: Amazon Bedrock's reinforcement fine-tuning accepts recorded invocation prompts as training data.
cards.explanation: Amazon Bedrock offers invocation logs as a training data source for reinforcement fine-tuning. Recorded requests supply prompts drawn from the application's actual usage.
cards.volatilityNote: Amazon Bedrock's reinforcement fine-tuning data-source options are evolving.

source.title: Customize a model with reinforcement fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock

cards.statement: ROUGE evaluates a generated summary's readability by comparing it with a reference summary.
cards.explanation: ROUGE checks words or word sequences shared by generated and reference summaries. It measures content overlap rather than readability or coherent phrasing.
cards.misconception: ROUGE measures summary readability instead of lexical overlap with reference summaries.

source.title: Evaluate the text summarization capabilities of LLMs for enhanced decision-making on AWS

cards.statement: BERTScore recognizes similarity between a generated summary and a reference that uses different wording.
cards.explanation: BERTScore compares contextual embeddings of tokens in generated and reference text. It credits similar meaning expressed through synonyms or paraphrases.

source.title: Evaluate the text summarization capabilities of LLMs for enhanced decision-making on AWS

cards.statement: Amazon Bedrock can use the generator's token probabilities as scores in LLM-as-a-judge evaluations.
cards.explanation: Amazon Bedrock uses a separate evaluator model to score the generator's responses against selected criteria. The evaluator also explains its scores.
cards.misconception: LLM-as-a-judge scores come from the response generator's token probabilities.

source.title: Evaluate model performance using another LLM as a judge

cards.statement: Human evaluators assess foundation model responses for alignment with a company's preferred brand voice.
cards.explanation: Human evaluation captures subjective preferences such as brand voice and creative intent. Reviewers use the business's evaluation instructions to judge the responses.

source.title: Amazon Bedrock FAQs — Model evaluation

cards.statement: An evaluation team reuses fine-tuning examples as test cases to measure performance on unfamiliar inputs.
cards.explanation: Teams keep evaluation data separate from fine-tuning data to protect measurement integrity. Testing known examples distorts evidence about performance on unfamiliar inputs.
cards.misconception: Testing on fine-tuning examples provides an independent assessment of unseen-input performance.

source.title: Identify the datasets needed for training and customizing your system

cards.statement: Amazon Bedrock automatic evaluations use different accuracy measures for summarization and question answering.
cards.explanation: Amazon Bedrock selects accuracy measures suited to the generation task. An accuracy result needs interpretation in the context of the task being evaluated.

source.title: Model evaluation task types in Amazon Bedrock

cards.statement: Amazon Bedrock retrieve-only RAG evaluations score the final answer written by a response generator.
cards.explanation: Amazon Bedrock evaluates retrieval quality from the retrieved information. A retrieve-only evaluation isolates that stage; response-generation quality belongs to the combined evaluation.
cards.misconception: Retrieve-only RAG evaluations score the response generator's final answer.

source.title: Evaluate the performance of RAG sources using Amazon Bedrock evaluations

cards.statement: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations scores tool choices in the context of an agent's conversation.
cards.explanation: AgentCore Evaluations assesses whether the selected tool serves the user's request at that point in the conversation, using the available tools and preceding context.
cards.volatilityNote: AgentCore evaluation capabilities and built-in criteria are evolving.

source.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore built-in evaluator prompt templates

cards.statement: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Observability shows intermediate steps along an agent's execution path.
cards.explanation: AgentCore Observability exposes workflow traces and intermediate outputs. Teams use this evidence to investigate bottlenecks and failures inside an agent's execution.
cards.volatilityNote: AgentCore observability features and telemetry integration are evolving.

source.title: Observe your agent applications on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Observability

cards.statement: An agent's task completion rate measures the proportion of individual tool calls that return successfully.
cards.explanation: Task completion evaluates whether the agent achieves the user's intended outcome across the workflow. A successful individual tool call can leave that outcome unfinished.
cards.misconception: Successful tool invocations count as completed user tasks.

source.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore built-in evaluator prompt templates

cards.statement: A model with cheaper calls can cost more per successful user task when it takes extra attempts.
cards.explanation: Cost per successful outcome includes spending on unsuccessful attempts. Retry frequency changes the cost of achieving an accepted result, so call price gives an incomplete comparison.

source.title: Beyond the price per token: Choosing the right OpenAI model on Amazon Bedrock for your workload

cards.statement: AI teams select fairness criteria independently of the use case and affected stakeholders.
cards.explanation: AI teams choose fairness criteria for the use case and affected stakeholders. Different fairness goals can conflict, so the choice depends on context.
cards.misconception: Fairness has a universal criterion that applies to different AI use cases.

source.title: Measure fairness as unwanted bias across stakeholder groups

cards.statement: AI robustness includes a model's behavior on adversarial inputs designed to mislead its predictions.
cards.explanation: Robustness concerns useful, reliable outputs under unexpected or adversarial inputs. Performance on ordinary inputs leaves this behavior untested.

source.title: Responsible AI: From principles to practice

cards.statement: AI teams can use prediction accuracy to measure agreement between a dataset's human annotators.
cards.explanation: Inter-rater agreement compares judgments made by different human labelers on the same examples. It measures labeling consistency rather than model prediction quality.
cards.misconception: Prediction accuracy measures agreement among human dataset annotators.

source.title: Validate the quality of human and generated labels and features in your dataset

cards.statement: AI teams infer demographic groups' error rates from a model's combined population-wide error rate.
cards.explanation: A population-wide error rate can conceal differences between demographic groups. Subgroup analysis examines performance separately for relevant groups.
cards.misconception: Overall model performance describes performance within demographic groups.

source.title: Measure fairness as unwanted bias across stakeholder groups

cards.statement: Human auditors check AI training data's factual claims against authoritative references and domain expertise.
cards.explanation: Human reviewers verify factual content using domain knowledge and reliable references. This review catches incorrect claims in data intended to teach a model.

source.title: Review the correctness of the content of your datasets

cards.statement: An overfitted model generalizes well to unseen data by fitting the random noise in its training examples.
cards.explanation: An overfitted model follows training-specific details, including noise, too closely. It can perform well on training examples yet poorly on unseen data.
cards.misconception: Learning random training noise helps a model generalize to unseen examples.

source.title: What is Overfitting?

cards.statement: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails can check both user text and model responses for harmful content.
cards.explanation: Content filters examine input prompts and model responses for harmful content such as hate or violence. Filtering strength is configurable for the application's needs.

source.title: Create your guardrail

cards.statement: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails uses AWS's fixed list of denied topics for a banking assistant.
cards.explanation: Customers define denied topics for their application's boundaries, such as investment advice for a banking assistant. The topic definition guides detection.
cards.misconception: AWS supplies a fixed denied-topic list for applications.

source.title: Block denied topics to help remove harmful content

cards.statement: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails word filters can block synonyms of a configured phrase through semantic similarity.
cards.explanation: Custom word filters match configured words and phrases exactly. A paraphrase or synonym needs its own matching entry to be blocked by that filter.
cards.misconception: Custom word filters recognize equivalent meanings rather than exact words or phrases.

source.title: Remove a specific list of words and phrases from conversations with word filters

cards.statement: AI teams choose smaller models that meet their quality needs to reduce the workload's energy demand.
cards.explanation: Right-sized models reduce unnecessary computational work while meeting the task's quality needs. Model selection therefore affects the environmental footprint of inference.

source.title: Leverage smaller models and optimized inference techniques to reduce carbon footprint

cards.statement: Model-generated content can expose a business to copyright infringement claims when it uses the output.
cards.explanation: Copyright claims can concern generated output, even when an AI model creates it. AI generation alone does not clear the rights of third parties.

source.title: Amazon Bedrock FAQs

cards.statement: SHAP assigns the probability that a model's predicted outcome is correct for the input it receives.
cards.explanation: SHAP estimates how input features contribute to a model's output relative to a baseline. These attributions describe influence rather than a prediction's probability of being correct.
cards.misconception: SHAP values are confidence scores for the correctness of a prediction.

source.title: What is Explainable AI?

cards.statement: Local explanations describe the factors driving a model's predictions across a customer population.
cards.explanation: Local explanations address an individual prediction. Global explanations summarize a model's behavior across multiple predictions.
cards.misconception: A local explanation describes the model's overall behavior across a population.

source.title: What is Explainable AI?

cards.statement: A post-hoc surrogate explanation directly reveals the original model's internal decision rules.
cards.explanation: A post-hoc surrogate approximates a model's input-output behavior. Its simplified rules describe that approximation rather than recovering the model's actual internal rules.
cards.misconception: A surrogate's explanation exposes the original model's actual internal rules.

source.title: What is Explainable AI?

cards.statement: AI transparency disclosures tell users when AI influences a decision that affects them.
cards.explanation: Disclosing AI involvement helps people make informed choices about engaging with a system. Users need to recognize where AI participates in decisions.

source.title: Identify potential harmful events impacting transparency

cards.statement: Explaining a model decision requires AI teams to protect sensitive training data from unauthorized access.
cards.explanation: Model explanations give users insight while preserving privacy. Sensitive training data stays protected from unauthorized access during explanation.

source.title: What is Explainable AI?

cards.statement: Developers use SageMaker Model Cards to record suitable production uses of a machine learning model.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Model Cards document the scenarios a model suits, development assumptions, and uses its developers discourage. This guides responsible adoption.

source.title: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards

cards.statement: AWS AI Service Cards certify that a customer's AI application meets its fairness requirements.
cards.explanation: AWS AI Service Cards explain intended uses, limitations, and responsible design choices for services and models. Customers assess their own application against its fairness requirements.
cards.misconception: AI Service Cards certify the fairness of customer applications built with a service.

source.title: Responsible AI Tools and Resources

cards.statement: Public access to a model's weights allows a business to use the model commercially.
cards.explanation: A model's license governs permitted use. Public availability does not establish commercial permission; users need to check the provider's applicable terms for their use case.
cards.misconception: Publicly accessible model weights imply permission for commercial use.

source.title: Model sources and license agreements

cards.statement: Using a cheaper approximation for a SHAP explanation can reduce the explanation's fidelity.
cards.explanation: Approximating feature attributions reduces computation but can make an explanation less faithful to the model. Explanation cost and fidelity form a trade-off.

source.title: Local interpretability

cards.statement: A counterfactual explanation shows what input edits would make a model return a different decision.
cards.explanation: Counterfactual explanations identify a small input change that changes a model's prediction. For a loan model, the alternative might involve a different income value.

source.title: Machine Learning Best Practices in Healthcare and Life Sciences — Model interpretability

cards.statement: Human-centered AI design includes channels through which users challenge a model's decisions.
cards.explanation: Feedback mechanisms let users contest AI outcomes after receiving them. This gives affected people a route to question and improve the system's behavior.

source.title: Map the user journey to identify AI interaction requirements
